# Hard stops (HS-v1)

These apply to every session, every role, every card. If a step would cross
one, stop the step, write what was needed in your return file with status
`BLOCKED`, and do nothing else for that step.

- **HS-1 Live data.** Never open, list, read, copy, back up, restore or
  query the live Apunta data folder, its backups, the owner's Claude export
  or Halaxy PDFs. Never contact port **7717**. Never run
  `scripts/recover-current-linux.mjs` or `scripts/smoke-live.mjs`.
- **HS-2 Isolation.** Every command that starts an Apunta server, opens a
  database or launches the app runs through `scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs` once
  card P0.3 is APPROVED. Before that, only non-launching edits and unit
  tests that use in-memory or temporary databases created by the test.
- **HS-3 Downloads.** Only items in `docs/v2/ACQUISITION.md`, by the rules
  there. Never pull an Ollama tag that already exists locally. Never
  remove or replace an Ollama model.
- **HS-4 Git.** Work only on `feature/v2`, starting from the base commit the
  coordinator gave you. Never merge into `main`, pull, rebase, reset,
  force-push, rewrite history, or change repository visibility. Stage
  explicit paths only.
- **HS-5 Secrets.** Never create, print, copy or commit a production
  signing key or password. Test keys live only inside a sandbox run folder.
- **HS-6 Network at runtime.** No new network access from `server/`, `web/`
  or `shared/`. The only runtime exceptions are model acquisition (existing)
  and the update check in the Tauri shell (contract C-UPD).
- **HS-7 Safety instruments.** Never loosen a scorer, guard, lock, test or
  threshold to make a result pass. Never change a threshold in
  `docs/v2/CONTRACTS.md`.
- **HS-8 Fabricated data only.** Fixtures, audio, screenshots and examples
  are fabricated. English uses the prototype's sample people; Spanish uses
  only names in `e2e/fixtures/eval-es/NAMES.md`.
- **HS-9 Protected paths.** Never edit `prototype/`. Never edit files outside
  your card's "May edit" list.
- **HS-10 Owner-only actions.** Never enable Spanish in release builds, write
  the owner's clinical verdict, publish a release, create GitHub secrets, or
  stop or inspect the live v1 instance.

# S2.5 Server messages by code, and the boot-error page

## Objective
Every server-produced sentence a person reads is rendered from a catalogue key
in the language of the request that produced it, and **no wire shape changes**:
the browser keeps receiving a finished `message` and never learns a code. The
kinds, enumerated so the sentence and the write scope below agree: the API error
bodies (`{ error, message, details }`), the **20** AI-failure messages the
server pushes as SSE `error` events, the refine-lock sentences appended to a
reply, the SSE `status` **and** `progress` frames, the import and backup
sentences, the two persisted server-written strings, and the boot-error page
with its two JSON bodies. The enabler is one new module,
`server/src/http/locale.ts`, that answers "which language is this request in"
— no server code reads a locale today, and `routes/settings.ts:41-44`
`storedLanguage` is private to that one route. Three points need that answer
and none of them can reach it today: the error handler, which is constructed
once, at `server/src/app.ts:120`; the providers, which are built in
`server/src/ai/index.ts:22-48` behind the streaming
signatures at `server/src/ai/types.ts:198-204` and the STT request at
`server/src/ai/types.ts:274` (`WhisperOptions` at `server/src/ai/whisper.ts:46`
is how the locale reaches it); and the real speech-to-text provider's
progress sentence, `server/src/ai/whisper.ts:475,508`. All four files are in
May edit for that one reason and nothing else (Fixed decision 3).

Out of scope, named so it is not argued later: everything the **browser**
writes (`web/src/**`, including `web/src/api/client.ts`, which is what puts a
server message on screen at `:60-75,119-122`, and `web/src/test/fakeApi.ts`'s
own English status strings at `:246,1037,1089,1248`); the two browser-side
English sentences in `web/src/lib/recorder.ts:48-56` and
`web/src/hooks/useDictation.ts:8-9`, which S2.4 dispositioned as English and
reported for a later card; and the **closed** `ApiErrorCodeSchema`, which stays
closed (Fixed decision 2).

  catalogue, the two LLM providers' message strings, `createProviders`' two
  constructions (`ai/index.ts:22-48`), the three `LlmProvider` streaming
  signatures (`ai/types.ts:198-204`) and the real speech-to-text provider's two
  progress strings (`whisper.ts:475,508`). Not this card's: the retry ladder,
  the parsers, the model picker, whisper's spawn, timeout, progress parsing and
  failure classification, the retractions, the job registry.
- Logs stay English and content-free, wherever they are written
  (`routes/chat.ts:627-629` `logBlocked` counts, `http/errors.ts:117,133`).
  The catalogues are for the screen, never for a log line and never for a
  pino field.
- `shared/src/job-context.ts` — this card consumes a locale, and does not
  build a `JobContext` (Fixed decision 3).
- `prototype/`; no dependency, no model, no download, no install (HS-3).

## Fixed decisions
1. **The server renders the message; the wire does not change.**
   `ApiErrorSchema` stays `{ error, message, details? }` and
   `GenerateErrorEventSchema` stays `{ code, message }`; `message` carries the
   sentence **already rendered** in the request's language and `error`/`code`
   stays the machine-readable field the client branches on. This is the whole
   reason `web/src/api/client.ts` needs no edit: `toError` at `:60-75` reads
   `parsed.data.message` and `errorMessage` at `:119-122` returns it verbatim,
   and both keep working. The alternative — code plus `params` rendered by the
   browser tab — is **rejected**: it needs a `params` field in
   `shared/src/errors.ts` and an edit to `web/src/api/client.ts`, which is
   S2.3/S2.4/S2.6 territory, and it would put a translation decision in the
   tab that has no locale of its own beyond the setting it already reads.
2. **One key per distinct sentence, and the code enum stays closed.**
   `errors.<code>` remains the key for a code's single generic sentence —
   S2.2's seed `errors.language_unavailable` keeps its key and its bytes
   exactly — and every *other* sentence gets `errors.<code>.<slug>`, a short
   kebab-case name for the reason: `errors.bad_request.format_not_found`,
   `errors.bad_request.wav_unreadable`, `errors.bad_request.import_patient_limit`,
   `errors.not_found.note_format`, `errors.storage_error.disk_full`. The
   namespace prefix is unchanged, so S2.2's reservation and its parity rule
   cover the new keys with no change to `MessageKey`. A sentence that cannot be
   told apart from its code's generic sentence without a new `ApiErrorCode` is
   a **stop**, not a new enum member: the enum is closed and this card does not
   open it. This is the rule that keeps "Upload 2 or 3 completed notes so
   Apunta can see what they have in common" from collapsing into "Something is
   wrong with that request" — one key per code cannot carry it, and ten codes
   are shared by dozens of sentences.
3. **Which language, and read from where.** A request that is **not** inside a
   job uses the stored `language` setting. A job — recording, transcription,
   draft, refine, plan, briefing, brainstorm — reads its locale **once, at the
   start**, and every sentence it produces afterwards (SSE `status` and
   `progress` frames, the appended notices, the persisted row, a retry's
   error) uses that captured value and never the setting as it stands later
   (C-LANG@1 rule 4's second sentence: "Retries, SSE and persistence use the
   captured context, never the current setting"). A **refine** is the rule's
   named exception: the target note's `notes.locale`
   (`migrations/008_locale.sql`), whatever the setting says and whatever
   language the instruction is typed in — C-LANG@1's own rejection example.
   The reader is `server/src/http/locale.ts` (new): it resolves the note's
   locale for a refine, the captured locale for a job, and the setting
   otherwise, and the read moves out of `routes/settings.ts:41-44` so both
   callers share it. This card does **not** construct a `JobContext`: that
   module's own docstring reserves construction for S5.4 (prompt set) and P4.3
   (speech model), and a route building one today would be guessing at both.
   Capturing the locale in the streaming route's closure is enough for the text
   this card renders, and a `JobContext` is a later card's wiring.
   **Where the answer has to be carried, and who renders a frame.** The answer
   is unreachable at three points, in four files, and each of the four is in
   May edit for that one reason and nothing more:
   `server/src/app.ts:120,150`, the single construction of the error handler
   that renders four bodies of its own, plus the not-found body beside it;
   `server/src/ai/index.ts:22-48` with `server/src/ai/types.ts:198-204`, the
   only two places a provider is built and the only three signatures that
   decide what a streaming call can see; and `server/src/ai/whisper.ts:475,508`,
   the production transcription frame, which the factory at `:40` hands that
   same captured locale to. A `status` frame is therefore rendered **by the
   provider**, from the locale it was given, and the route forwards the
   finished sentence untouched (`routes/draft.ts:105-106`,
   `routes/transcribe.ts:327`) — it does not re-render. The `stage` cannot be
   the key, and the route cannot take the job over: `status('drafting',
   'Drafting the note…')` at `ollama.ts:971` and `status('drafting',
   'Thinking…')` at `fake.ts:303,312` are the same `GenerateStage` with two
   different sentences, so a route rendering from the stage would put the wrong
   one on screen. A thrown `HttpError` still renders in its route, which
   already holds `db`; only the handler's own four bodies and the `:150`
   not-found body need the wiring at `app.ts`.
4. **The boot-error page shows both languages, English first, and its two JSON
   bodies show English.** The page cannot read settings — storage is what
   failed — so `bootErrorHtml` renders the English sentence and then the
   Spanish one under `<html lang="en">`, in that order. The JSON bodies
   (`/api/health` and the not-found handler, `boot-error.ts:39-46`) cannot be
   bilingual and nothing in the browser is alive to ask: they carry
   `error: 'storage_error'` with the **English** sentence. `storageBootMessage`
   and the two `storageErrorFor` sentences stop interpolating `dataDir` and
   `dbFile` into a literal and return a code plus parameters instead
   (`errors.storage_error.disk_full` with `{dir}`,
   `errors.storage_error.read_only` with `{dir}`,
   `errors.storage_error.cannot_open` with `{file}`), which is what
   `server/src/index.ts:57-58` consumes.
5. **Persisted server text, and its legacy rule.**
   - `settings.last_backup_error` is stored from now on as a JSON object —
     `{ code, params, at }`, `at` the ISO stamp — instead of a string that is
     two things joined by an em dash. The **wire** field stays
     `z.string().nullable()` (`shared/src/backup.ts:221`) because the server
     renders it in the request's language inside `GET /api/backup`, so
     `BackupCard.tsx:210` and `shared/src/backup.ts` do not change; the stamp
     stays visible because the key declares `at` as a `date` parameter. A row
     that is **not** that object — any row written before this card, recognised
     by its ` — ` — is **displayed exactly as stored**: never re-rendered,
     never re-translated, never rewritten. No migration deletes or rewrites a
     stored row.
   - The persisted refine notices (`routes/chat.ts:610-623` `persistReply`)
     and `FIRST_PASS_MESSAGE` are rendered **at write time** in the target
     note's locale and stored as text, because C-LANG@1 rule 4 makes
     persistence use the captured context. Rows already stored are displayed
     as stored, on the same rule.
   - Import batch reports are **not** in this rule: they persist no text
     (`004_import_batches.sql:10-15` is `(id, source, created_at)`,
     `ImportBatchSchema` computes its counts live, and the report is rebuilt
     per request), so the rule that was written about them has nothing to say
     about them. The sentences an import **fails** with are ordinary 400s and
     are covered by decisions 1 and 2.
6. **English is unchanged.** Every English value this card writes is the string
   the server sends today, character for character (S2.2's FD6, C-LANG@1 rules
   3 and 5). A key whose English is not what the wire carries today is a stop,
   not a copy improvement — S2.7 and S2.8 own the copy. The existing
   assertions are the oracle and stay: `shared/src/chat.test.ts:38-39,44-45`,
   `server/src/routes/settings.test.ts:149`,
   `server/src/boot-error.test.ts:12`, and `server/src/app.test.ts:50`, which
   pins the `Not Found` body this card now renders at `app.ts:150`.
7. **The catalogues are the only place a sentence is written.** A new sentence
   lands in `en.ts` and `es-MX.ts` together or not at all; a key `es-MX.ts`
   lacks is a `tsc` error (S2.2's FD2 `satisfies` clause) and a key whose
   `es-MX` placeholders differ is a `t.test.ts` failure — **not** a `tsc`
   error, because `Message.text` is a `string` (`t.ts:16-32`). A key this card
   cannot fill with a real es-MX string is **reported, not filled with the
   English** (S2.4's FD6, same rule, same reason).
8. **Tests reach the Spanish state through the switch the API honours.**
   `vi.stubEnv('APUNTA_DEV_SPANISH', '1')` in `beforeEach` with
   `vi.unstubAllEnvs()` in `afterEach` — the pattern
   `shared/src/i18n/t.test.ts` already uses — so `PUT /api/settings
   { language: 'es-MX' }` is accepted (`routes/settings.ts:30-32,81-85`);
   writing the `settings` row directly through the harness is the equivalent
   and is allowed. No test enables Spanish by another route.

## Stop conditions
- A user-visible server sentence in a file this card does not own — anything in
  `web/src/**`, in `server/src/ai/` beyond the entries May edit names, or in
  a `server/src` file missing from May edit — is a `BLOCKED` return naming its
  `file:line`. May edit is not widened (HS-9). The known cases are the browser's
  own English status strings (`web/src/test/fakeApi.ts:246,1037,1089,1248`) and
  the two recorder/hook sentences S2.4 dispositioned; they stay English and are
  reported as findings for S2.6.
- A render site in one of the four files May edit line-pins, where the card
  does not name it — a second sentence in `app.ts` outside `:120,150`; a third
  `progress` `message` in `whisper.ts` outside `:475,508`; a fourth streaming
  method on `LlmProvider` (`ai/types.ts`); a provider built anywhere but
  `ai/index.ts:22-48` — is a `BLOCKED` return naming the `file:line` and the
  sentence. Those four files are licensed for the wiring and nothing more, and
  widening them is this coordinator's call, not the implementer's (HS-9). The
  same response covers a render site that would need a **new** SSE `LlmEvent`
  variant: the union's shape is not this card's.
- A change to guard **logic** — a branch, a count, a threshold, a logged field,
  or anything that decides whether to block — is a `BLOCKED` return naming the
  `file:line`. Localising a notice's words is this card's; deciding *whether* to
  block, *what* to count and *what to log* is not, and the guards are not
  touched.
- A `tsc` error or a red assertion in a file this card does not own — the
  likely one is `shared/src/chat.test.ts:38-39,44-45` if the two constants
  change shape without that file moving — is a `BLOCKED` return with the
  compiler output. Do not make a field optional to quiet the compiler and do
  not relax an assertion (HS-7).
- A sentence that cannot be keyed without a **new** `ApiErrorCode` — i.e.
  without editing the closed `ApiErrorCodeSchema` (`shared/src/errors.ts:4-29`)
  — is a `BLOCKED` return naming the sentence, the `file:line` and the code it
  would need. The enum is not opened here, and a second sentence under an
  existing code gets its own `errors.<code>.<slug>` key instead (Fixed
  decision 2).
- A catalogue entry this card cannot fill with a real es-MX string, or one
  whose `es-MX` placeholder set differs from its English twin: **stop** and
  name the key, both texts and the file. The English is not shipped as Spanish
  (Fixed decision 7), the placeholder is not dropped to make the set match, and
  the mismatch is left for V1's parity case to fail on, never for a row to be
  narrowed around.
- A stored row that predates this card and cannot be displayed **as stored** —
  a `last_backup_error` that is neither the new object nor a parseable legacy
  string, or a persisted notice whose stored locale is unknown — is a
  `BLOCKED` return naming the row's shape. No migration deletes, rewrites or
  re-renders stored text, and a legacy row is shown byte for byte as it stands.

# Contract excerpts (authoritative)

## C-LANG@1 Language, documents and jobs

**Built by** S2.1. **Proven by** S2.6, S4b.1, S5.6. **Consumers:** web,
server routes, AI prompts, guards, speech, spell check, formats, backup.

1. Setting `language` ∈ `en` | `es-MX`, default `en`. The server exposes
   `spanishAvailable: boolean`: true only when `APUNTA_DEV_SPANISH=1` (D12).
   When false, the Language control is hidden and `es-MX` is rejected by
   `PUT /api/settings` with code `language_unavailable`.
2. Locale mapping (one table in `shared/src/i18n/locales.ts`):

   | App | UI and `Intl` | Whisper `-l` | Speech model | Dictionary | Prompts |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | `en` | unchanged from today | `en` | `ggml-tiny.en.bin` | current English | current |
   | `es-MX` | `es-MX` | `es` | per C-STT selection | per S1.5 | Spanish set |

3. Documents: migration adds `locale TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'en'` to notes
   and to formats. **All existing rows are `en`.** New notes take the job's
   locale. Existing notes and formats are never translated or relabelled.
4. Jobs capture `{ locale, sttModel, llmModel, promptSet }` at start
   (recording, transcription, draft, refine, plan, briefing, brainstorm).
   Retries, SSE and persistence use the captured context, never the current
   setting. **Refine uses the target note's locale**, whatever the UI
   language and whatever language the request is typed in.
5. Section roles: `shared/src/section-roles.ts` maps known section names in
   both languages (case- and accent-insensitive) to role IDs (`location`,
   `presentation`, `risk`, `discussion`, `intervention`, `actions`,
   `next_session`, and the SOAP and intake roles). Guards use roles, not
   strings. Unknown sections get role `custom`. Stored strings are not
   rewritten.
6. Changing Language is blocked while any job or save is active: the web
   control is disabled with a reason; the server also returns 409
   `language_change_blocked` if it knows of an active job.
7. Spanish dictation requires the Spanish speech model to be ready (C-ACQ).
   If it is not, dictation shows "Spanish speech model not installed" with
   a download action. **Spanish audio is never sent to the English model.**
8. The Spanish standard format is created as a separate format with
   `locale: 'es-MX'`; English formats are untouched. Imported formats take
   the UI language at import time; the user can change a format's locale.
9. Backups and restores carry the `locale` columns.

**Rejection example.** UI switched to Español, user refines an existing
English note with a Spanish instruction → the note stays English, the reply
explains the change in the note's language.

# Run configuration (v2 plan)

## 1. Ports

| Use | Port |
| --- | --- |
| Live instance: **never contact** | 7717 |
| Sandbox servers (C-ISO) | 7800 to 7889 |
| Updater test server (C-UPD) | 7890 to 7899 |
| Playwright under the sandbox | the port `sandbox.mjs env` assigns |

## 2. Gate levels

A card names one level. Commands run from the repository root unless a card
says otherwise. Until P0.3 is APPROVED, only L0 and the non-launching part of
L1 may run.

| Level | When | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **L0** docs only | cards that change only Markdown | `npx prettier --check <changed files>`; `node scripts/check-no-external-urls.mjs` |
| **L1** targeted | every implementation card | `npm run lint`; `npm run typecheck`; `npm run build:shared`, then the card's named test files with `npx vitest run <paths>` from the repository root (the root `vitest.config.ts` defines the projects) |
| **L2** parent acceptance | every parent review card | everything in §3 |
| **L3** native or real model | cards and parent reviews that say so | the card's listed commands, all through `sandbox.mjs` |

## 3. The L2 suite

```sh
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
TZ=UTC npm test
TZ=America/Denver npm test
TZ=America/Mexico_City npm test
TZ=Australia/Sydney npm test
npm run build
node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs env --port 7810 > /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && . /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && npm run e2e
npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1
```

After P0.2, each `TZ=` run prints its effective zone (a test asserts it), so
four runs really exercise four zones. After P0.3, the e2e line is the only
permitted way to run Playwright. After S3.2, add
